# Re-key Migration (MM-411) — Frontend Reconnaissance

**Base path:** `apps/identity-wallet/src` (all paths below are relative to it unless absolute).

**Architectural headline:** The whole wallet is a **single-component state machine** driven by one `step` variable in `routes/+page.svelte`, not by SvelteKit routes. There is no store singleton for identities — the "identity list world" is loaded imperatively inside `IdentityListHome.svelte` from Rust IPC. Existing flows (create ceremony, migration, removal) are already modeled as step sequences with resume-on-launch reconciliation. A re-key flow slots in as new `OnboardingStep` values plus new components, mirroring the migration/removal patterns.

---

## 1. IdentityStore (frontend)

There is **no dedicated Svelte store**. The wired-in identity list lives as `$state` local to the home component and is hydrated from Rust.

- **IPC surface — `lib/ipc/identity.ts`:**
  - `listIdentities(): Promise<string[]>` → `invoke('list_identities')` (identity.ts:13). **The list is bare DID strings only** — no rich record.
  - `getStoredDidDoc(did): Promise<Record<string,unknown> | null>` → `invoke('get_stored_did_doc')` (identity.ts:16).
  - `refreshDidDoc(did)` → `invoke('refresh_did_doc')` (identity.ts:25) — re-fetches the PLC data doc; used to self-heal caches missing `rotationKeys`.
  - `getDeviceKeyId(did): Promise<string>` → `invoke('get_device_key_id')` (identity.ts:28).
  - `IdentityStoreError` union (identity.ts:6-11): `IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND | IDENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS | KEYCHAIN_ERROR | KEY_GENERATION_FAILED | SERIALIZATION_ERROR`.

- **The composed frontend record** is `interface IdentityCard` — defined **inline** in `IdentityListHome.svelte:35-40`:
  ```ts
  interface IdentityCard { did; handle: string|null; pdsUrl: string|null; deviceKeyIsRoot: boolean|null; }
  ```
  Built in `loadData()` (IdentityListHome.svelte:68-128): for each DID it `Promise.all([getStoredDidDoc, getDeviceKeyId])`, self-heals via `refreshDidDoc` when `docNeedsRotationKeysRefresh` (line 87), then derives `handle`/`pdsUrl`/`deviceKeyIsRoot`.

- **did:plc vs did:web:** Not stored as a field — it is **derived from the DID string** via `isDidWeb(did)` (`lib/did-doc-utils.ts:100`, method-segment check). did:web has no rotation keys, so the badge switches (IdentityListHome.svelte:254).

- **rotationKeys / recovery state:** The DID doc carries `rotationKeys` (a flat string array, PLC data shape). The only derived signal is **`deviceKeyIsRoot`**: `isDeviceKeyRoot()` (IdentityListHome.svelte:59-66) returns `rotationKeys[0] === deviceKeyId` (true/false/null). **This is the exact seam for a re-key prompt** — an existing account whose device key is *not* `rotationKeys[0]`, or whose recovery/rotation-key set is stale, is what MM-411 wants to detect. Note `docNeedsRotationKeysRefresh` (did-doc-utils.ts:41) already flags docs cached before rotationKeys existed.

---

## 2. Home surface

**`lib/components/home/IdentityListHome.svelte`** — the main list screen.

- Props (lines 19-33): `onadd`, `onselect(did, didDoc, deviceKeyIsRoot)`, `onalert?`, `onagents?`, `onsettings?`. Callbacks bubble to `+page.svelte`, which owns navigation.
- **Per-identity state rendering** happens in the `{#each identities as card}` block (lines 244-290). Each card is a `.card-group` containing the main `<button class="card">` plus an optional stacked `.alert-strip` (lines 282-288) fused to the card bottom when `alertData.get(card.did)` has unauthorized changes.
- **Where a re-key prompt hooks in:** The `.alert-strip` pattern (lines 282-288) is the precedent for a per-identity call-to-action strip fused under a card. A calm "upgrade available" banner would mirror this but use `--color-seal-tint`/accent tones (the "reveal the machinery" aubergine) rather than `--color-critical-surface`. There is also a top-of-list `.monitor` banner (lines 207-239) with three tonal variants (`--safe` green, `--web` aubergine, `--alert` critical) — the `monitor--web` variant is the exact "calm, informational, non-alarmist" tone MM-411 wants.

---

## 3. ShamirBackupScreen (reusable Share 3 custody)

**`lib/components/onboarding/ShamirBackupScreen.svelte`** — walks the user through saving Share 3 with confirm-before-continue.

- **Props (lines 6-26):**
  - `share3: string` — machine form (base32 envelope), the QR payload.
  - `share3Words?: string` (default `''`) — BIP-39-style word phrase, primary human rendering; empty falls back to formatted machine form.
  - `confirmError?: string | null` — failure from the parent's confirm step (biometric/teardown), rendered inline; user retries via same button.

- **Reuse for re-key:** directly reusable. The re-key epilogue will produce a fresh Share 3 (new recovery seed) and needs the identical custody confirmation. You feed it the new `share3`/`share3Words` and wire `oncomplete` to your re-key confirm/teardown.

---

## 1. `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share` handler

**File:** `crates/pds/src/routes/recovery_escrow.rs`
**Handler:** `put_escrow_share` — `recovery_escrow.rs:81-155`

**Auth** (`recovery_escrow.rs:88`): `authenticate_owner(...)` → wraps `auth::guards::authenticate_account_owner` (`recovery_escrow.rs:43-62`). Accepts a wallet **session token OR full-access OAuth/XRPC token**; **refuses agent-derived and app-password credentials** (`OwnerAuthError::AgentDerived` → InsufficientScope, `NotFullAccess` → InvalidToken). Returns the caller's DID string.

**Request body** (`recovery_escrow.rs:69-73`): `PutEscrowShareRequest { share: String }` — the base32 v2 share envelope.

**What it does:**
1. Decodes/validates the envelope — `crypto::ShareEnvelope::decode_share` (`recovery_escrow.rs:93`); rejects if `envelope.index() != 2` (`ESCROW_SHARE_INDEX`, `recovery_escrow.rs:65,95-100`).
2. KEK-wraps via `crypto::encrypt_secret_bytes(envelope.to_bytes(), master_key)` (`recovery_escrow.rs:113`); master key from `state.config.signing_key_master_key`, else 503 (`recovery_escrow.rs:102-112`).
3. Opens a tx (`recovery_escrow.rs:126`); branches on `escrow_share_exists`:
   - exists → `replace_escrow_share` → event `Rotated` (`:127-131`)
   - new → `insert_escrow_share` → event `Deposited` (`:132-137`)
4. Appends `recovery_audit_events` row with `detail = {set_id, version}` (`:138-149`), commits (`:150`).

**DB write path** — `crates/pds/src/db/recovery_escrow.rs`:
- `insert_escrow_share` (`db/recovery_escrow.rs:29-46`): `INSERT INTO recovery_escrow (did, share_encrypted, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, datetime('now'))`.
- `replace_escrow_share` (`db/recovery_escrow.rs:53-74`): `UPDATE recovery_escrow SET share_encrypted=?, rotated_at=datetime('now'), release_requested_at=NULL, release_pending_until=NULL WHERE did=?` (a replacement voids any pending release).
- `escrow_share_exists` (`db/recovery_escrow.rs:18-26`), `delete_escrow_share` (`db/recovery_escrow.rs:79-88`).

All generic over the sqlx executor, so the handler composes them with the audit insert in one tx.

## 2. `recovery_escrow` table + legacy `accounts.recovery_share`

**Migration creating `recovery_escrow`:** `crates/pds/src/db/migrations/V050__recovery_escrow.sql`
- Table `recovery_escrow` (`V050:16-23`): `did TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(did)`, `share_encrypted TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `rotated_at TEXT`, `release_requested_at TEXT`, `release_pending_until TEXT`, `WITHOUT ROWID`.

**Legacy column:** `crates/pds/src/db/migrations/V010__recovery_shares.sql:13` — `ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN recovery_share TEXT;` (base32 Share 2, NULL for pre-Shamir accounts).

**Where to add the §7 null-out (legacy column) on a successful escrow deposit:**
The natural insertion point is inside the `put_escrow_share` transaction in `recovery_escrow.rs`, after the insert/replace + audit event and **before `tx.commit()` at `recovery_escrow.rs:150`** (e.g. right after line 149). ## 3. KEK wrapping / SecretFamily

**File:** `crates/pds/src/db/kek.rs`

The escrowed Share 2 is AES-256-GCM wrapped with `crypto::encrypt_secret_bytes(..., master_key)` (called at `recovery_escrow.rs:113` and `create_did.rs:343`) — the shared `base64(nonce || ciphertext || tag)` `SecretFamily` envelope (`kek.rs:139-147`).

**Both columns ARE registered SecretFamily variants** (`kek.rs:23-47`, `SecretFamily::ALL` has 9 entries, `kek.rs:51-61`):

## 5. `plc_monitor` (tamper detection) — in the identity-wallet app, not the PDS

**File:** `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/plc_monitor.rs`

**Authorization logic** — `PlcMonitor::check_for_changes` (`plc_monitor.rs:89-175`):
1. Fetches the plc.directory audit log (`plc_monitor.rs:94`), parses (`parse_audit_log`, `:102`), diffs against the cached log (`diff_audit_logs`, `:128`) to get only **new** entries.
2. Loads the wallet's device key for the DID (`get_or_create_device_key`, `:136-142`).
3. For each new entry (`:146-167`): **an op is "authorized" iff it verifies against the wallet's own device key** —
   `if verify_plc_operation(&op_json, std::slice::from_ref(&device_key_uri)).is_ok() { continue; }` (`plc_monitor.rs:153`). Otherwise it becomes an `UnauthorizedChange` (`:161-166`), and `identify_signing_key` (`:179-206`) tries to name the signer by testing each `rotationKeys` entry from the **previous** op.

**Key point for the acceptance criterion:** The authorization check is purely **"did OUR device key sign this op?"** — it does NOT compare against a list of known/expected rotationKeys, and it does NOT special-case what the op *does* (adding a recovery key, changing rotationKeys, etc.). It only checks the **signature**. So:

> A re-key op **signed by the device key** (the device key being at `rotationKeys[0]`, or any position — position is irrelevant to the check) verifies at `plc_monitor.rs:153` and is treated as **authorized → no tamper alert.** ✅

This is exactly what the test `test_ac6_1_authorized_change_detected` (`plc_monitor.rs:421-469`) asserts: a genesis op signed by the device key (even when the device key is `rotationKeys[1]` and a separate key is `rotationKeys[0]`, `:433-441`) produces zero alerts. The device-key signature — not the key's position or the op's contents — is the sole authorization criterion. A device-key-signed rotation op that inserts a recovery key will therefore verify and be authorized.

(Server-side `crypto::verify_plc_operation` lives in `crates/crypto/src/plc.rs`; the wallet-side recovery/fork logic that consumes these alerts is `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/recovery.rs`.)

1	// pattern: Mixed (Functional Core guard/diff; Imperative Shell build/submit commands)
2	//
3	// Functional Core: the strict rotation guard and the review-diff computation (pure).
4	// Imperative Shell: build_repo_key_rotation / submit_repo_key_rotation (network +
5	//                   Keychain + signing) and their Tauri command wrappers.
6	//
7	// This is the sovereign "rotate repo signing key" flow for a wallet-custodied did:plc
8	// identity. The PDS-held repo signing key (`verificationMethods.atproto`, also the PDS
9	// slot in `rotationKeys` — the key that signs every repo commit) can be compromised
10	// (attacker read the PDS database and master key) or lost (master key gone). Either way
11	// the fix is a FRESH key, and only the wallet can authorize it: the PDS's own key is the
12	// exact key being replaced, while the wallet device key at `rotationKeys[0]` outranks it.
13	//
14	// The two existing wallet guards both forbid this op — migration must move `services`
15	// and recovery must change nothing — so this module is a FOURTH allowlist, scoped to
16	// exactly one mutation: `verificationMethods.atproto` and the PDS `rotationKeys` slot
17	// move to a key the hosting PDS just staged; everything else must be preserved.
18	//
19	// The flow is fully passwordless end to end (sovereign login + the per-DID session
20	// provider supply the full-access session; the biometric gate lives in the frontend,
21	// in front of the Secure-Enclave signing):
22	//   1. Resolve a full-access session for the DID via SessionProvider.
23	//   2. `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation` on the hosting PDS — it stages a fresh key and
24	//      returns the `did:key` id the op must install.
25	//   3. Build + device-key-sign the rotation op (strict guard) — but do NOT POST it to
26	//      plc.directory: the signed op goes back to the PDS.
27	//   4. `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation/complete` — the PDS submits the op to plc.directory
28	//      and cuts its commit signer over under the account's repo write lock, so no
29	//      commit is ever signed by a key absent from the DID document. (This is why the
30	//      wallet must not submit this op itself, unlike the recovery/migration legs.)
31	//   5. Refresh the cached PLC log + DID document so the home card updates.
32	//
33	// The PDS `complete` endpoint is retry-safe (an op that already landed skips the
34	// re-submit and just cuts over), so a lost response is healed by re-running submit.
35

47	/// The atproto verification-method id in a PLC operation's `verificationMethods` map.
48	const ATPROTO_VERIFICATION_METHOD_ID: &str = "atproto";

50	// ── Errors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	
52	/// Errors from the sovereign repo signing-key rotation flow.
53	///
54	/// Serializes as `{ "code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", ... }` to match the sibling
55	/// wallet error enums (`MigrateError`, `RecoveryError`, `HandleChangeError`).
56	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
57	#[serde(
58	    tag = "code",
59	    rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE",
60	    rename_all_fields = "camelCase"
61	)]
62	pub enum RotationError {
63	    /// The wallet holds no authorized key in the DID's current rotationKeys, so it
64	    /// cannot self-sign the rotation op.
65	    #[error("wallet is not authorized to self-sign for this DID (no device key in current rotationKeys)")]
66	    WalletNotAuthorized,
67	    /// The identity's session could not be resolved without a passwordless unlock —
68	    /// the frontend should run the biometric sovereign login and retry.
69	    #[error("identity is locked and needs a passwordless unlock")]
70	    SessionLocked { reason: UnlockReason },
71	    /// The hosting PDS or plc.directory rate limited the request.
72	    #[error("rate limited")]
73	    RateLimited { retry_after: Option<String> },
74	    /// The strict pre-sign allowlist rejected the proposed operation.
75	    #[error("rotation operation rejected by pre-sign guard: {reason}")]
76	    GuardRejected { reason: String },
77	    /// The audit log could not be parsed or contained no usable current state.
78	    #[error("invalid audit log: {message}")]
79	    InvalidAuditLog { message: String },
80	    /// Local signing failed.
81	    #[error("signing failed: {message}")]
82	    SigningFailed { message: String },
83	    /// The hosting PDS rejected a rotation call for a reason the wallet does not
84	    /// model specifically.
85	    #[error("rotation request failed (HTTP {status}): {message}")]
86	    RotationFailed { status: u16, message: String },
87	    /// A network / transport call failed.
88	    #[error("network error: {message}")]
89	    NetworkError { message: String },
90	    /// The DID's device key or identity record could not be found.
91	    #[error("identity not found: {message}")]
92	    IdentityNotFound { message: String },
93	    /// No built rotation op is pending for this DID (build must run first).
94	    #[error("no rotation operation is pending")]
95	    NoPendingRotation,
96	}

98	/// Map a session-lifecycle failure into the rotation surface. A needed unlock stays a
99	/// distinct, actionable signal; a rate limit is preserved; everything else degrades to
100	/// a transport error the frontend can retry.
101	fn map_session_error(error: SessionError) -> RotationError {
102	    match error {
103	        SessionError::NeedsUnlock { reason } => RotationError::SessionLocked { reason },
104	        SessionError::RateLimited { retry_after } => RotationError::RateLimited { retry_after },
105	        SessionError::IdentityNotFound => RotationError::IdentityNotFound {
106	            message: "identity not found".to_string(),
107	        },
108	        SessionError::Offline { message } => RotationError::NetworkError { message },
109	        other => RotationError::NetworkError {
110	            message: other.to_string(),
111	        },
112	    }
113	}

115	// ── Pure inputs to the guard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
116	
117	/// The facts the strict pre-sign guard needs to decide whether a proposed rotation is
118	/// safe to sign. Flattened to plain values so the guard is a pure, trivially-testable
119	/// function (mirrors `HandleChangeInputs` / `MigrationInputs`).
120	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
121	pub struct RotationInputs {
122	    /// The wallet's per-DID device key (`did:key:z...`). Must be in the current set.
123	    pub device_key_id: String,
124	    /// The replacement key the hosting PDS staged (`did:key:z...`) — the ONLY key that
125	    /// may enter the DID document through this flow.
126	    pub staged_key_id: String,
127	    /// The DID's CURRENT rotation keys (from the latest audit-log op).
128	    pub current_rotation_keys: Vec<String>,
129	    /// The rotation keys we intend to put in the op.
130	    pub proposed_rotation_keys: Vec<String>,
131	    /// The DID's CURRENT verificationMethods.
132	    pub current_verification_methods: BTreeMap<String, String>,
133	    /// The verificationMethods we intend to put in the op.
134	    pub proposed_verification_methods: BTreeMap<String, String>,
135	    /// The DID's CURRENT services — must be preserved unchanged.
136	    pub current_services: BTreeMap<String, PlcService>,
137	    /// The services we intend to put in the op — must EQUAL the current.
138	    pub proposed_services: BTreeMap<String, PlcService>,
139	    /// The DID's CURRENT alsoKnownAs — must be preserved unchanged.
140	    pub current_also_known_as: Vec<String>,
141	    /// The alsoKnownAs we intend to put in the op — must EQUAL the current.
142	    pub proposed_also_known_as: Vec<String>,
143	}
144	
145	// ── The strict pre-sign guard (STRICT ALLOWLIST) ─────────────────────────────
146	
147	/// Reject the proposed rotation operation unless it satisfies the strict allowlist.
148	/// This is the security core of the flow: the device key can technically sign
149	/// anything, so safety comes entirely from validating the INPUTS before a signature
150	/// is produced.
151	///
152	/// The allowlist: the atproto verification method and the PDS `rotationKeys` slot move
153	/// to the PDS-staged key — nothing else may change.
154	///
155	/// Rules:
156	///  1. Authorization: `device_key_id` is present in `current_rotation_keys`.
157	///  2. Freshness: the staged key differs from the device key and from every current
158	///     rotation key / the current atproto method (a "rotation" to an already-installed
159	///     key would be a no-op signed for nothing).
160	///  3. Sovereignty: `proposed_rotation_keys` is exactly `[device_key_id, staged_key_id]`
161	///     — the device key stays at index 0 (ADR-0001), the staged key takes the PDS slot,
162	///     and no other key can ride along.
163	///  4. Verification methods: `proposed_verification_methods` equals the current map
164	///     with ONLY the `atproto` entry replaced by the staged key.
165	///  5. Services unchanged: a rotation must not move the account off its PDS.
166	///  6. alsoKnownAs unchanged: a rotation must not touch the handle set.
167	pub fn guard_rotation_op(inputs: &RotationInputs) -> Result<(), RotationError> {
168	    // Rule 1 (authorization): checked first so the distinct `WalletNotAuthorized`
169	    // signal wins over any proposed-op quibble.
170	    if !inputs.current_rotation_keys.contains(&inputs.device_key_id) {
171	        return Err(RotationError::WalletNotAuthorized);
172	    }
173	
174	    // Rule 2 (freshness).
175	    if inputs.staged_key_id == inputs.device_key_id {
176	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
177	            reason: "staged key must not be the device key".to_string(),
178	        });
179	    }
180	    if inputs.current_rotation_keys.contains(&inputs.staged_key_id)
181	        || inputs
182	            .current_verification_methods
183	            .get(ATPROTO_VERIFICATION_METHOD_ID)
184	            == Some(&inputs.staged_key_id)
185	    {
186	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
187	            reason: "staged key is already installed in the DID document".to_string(),
188	        });
189	    }
190	
191	    // Rule 3 (sovereignty + no smuggled keys).
192	    let expected_keys = vec![inputs.device_key_id.clone(), inputs.staged_key_id.clone()];
193	    if inputs.proposed_rotation_keys != expected_keys {
194	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
195	            reason: "rotationKeys must be exactly [device key, staged key]".to_string(),
196	        });
197	    }
198	
199	    // Rule 4 (verification methods: only the atproto entry moves, to the staged key).
200	    let mut expected_vms = inputs.current_verification_methods.clone();
201	    expected_vms.insert(
202	        ATPROTO_VERIFICATION_METHOD_ID.to_string(),
203	        inputs.staged_key_id.clone(),
204	    );
205	    if inputs.proposed_verification_methods != expected_vms {
206	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
207	            reason: "verificationMethods may only replace the atproto entry with the staged key"
208	                .to_string(),
209	        });
210	    }
211	
212	    // Rule 5 (services unchanged): the atproto_pds endpoint must not move.
213	    if inputs.proposed_services != inputs.current_services {
214	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
215	            reason: "services must be preserved across a key rotation".to_string(),
216	        });
217	    }
218	
219	    // Rule 6 (alsoKnownAs unchanged).
220	    if inputs.proposed_also_known_as != inputs.current_also_known_as {
221	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {
222	            reason: "alsoKnownAs must be preserved across a key rotation".to_string(),
223	        });
224	    }
225	
226	    Ok(())
227	}
228	
229	// ── Review diff ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
230	
231	/// Compute the review-screen diff for a rotation: the staged key enters, every current
232	/// rotation key / atproto method not carried forward leaves, services never change.
233	/// Pure.
234	pub(crate) fn build_rotation_diff(
235	    current_rotation_keys: &[String],
236	    current_atproto_key: Option<&str>,
237	    proposed_rotation_keys: &[String],
238	    staged_key_id: &str,
239	    prev_cid: &str,
240	) -> OpDiff {
241	    let mut removed_keys: Vec<String> = current_rotation_keys
242	        .iter()
243	        .filter(|k| !proposed_rotation_keys.contains(k))
244	        .cloned()
245	        .collect();
246	    // The outgoing atproto method may not have been in rotationKeys at all (a
247	    // non-canonical document); it is still being removed from the document.
248	    if let Some(old_atproto) = current_atproto_key {
249	        if old_atproto != staged_key_id
250	            && !removed_keys.iter().any(|k| k == old_atproto)
251	            && !proposed_rotation_keys.iter().any(|k| k == old_atproto)
252	        {
253	            removed_keys.push(old_atproto.to_string());
254	        }
255	    }
256	    OpDiff {
257	        added_keys: vec![staged_key_id.to_string()],
258	        removed_keys,
259	        changed_services: Vec::new(),
260	        prev_cid: Some(prev_cid.to_string()),
261	    }
262	}
263	
264	// ── Output types / pending state ─────────────────────────────────────────────
265	
266	/// A rotation operation, built and signed locally, ready to hand to the PDS.
267	///
268	/// Mirrors `SignedRecoveryOp`: the `diff` drives the review / biometric-approval UI,
269	/// and `signed_op` is the JSON the PDS will submit to plc.directory.
270	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Clone)]
271	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
272	pub struct SignedRotationOp {
273	    /// Human-readable diff of what the rotation changes (the key swap).
274	    pub diff: OpDiff,
275	    /// The signed PLC operation JSON, submitted via the PDS `complete` endpoint.
276	    pub signed_op: serde_json::Value,
277	}
278	
279	/// State for a pending rotation, held between build and submit (mirrors
280	/// `RecoveryState`).
281	pub struct RotationState {
282	    /// The DID being rotated.
283	    pub did: String,
284	    /// The signed PLC op, set by `build_repo_key_rotation_cmd`. Kept parked across a
285	    /// failed submit (the PDS `complete` endpoint is retry-safe); cleared on success.
286	    pub signed_op: serde_json::Value,
287	}
288	
289	// ── PDS rotation endpoints ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
290	
291	/// Read an atproto-style error envelope `{ error, message }` from a non-success
292	/// response and map it into a `RotationError`.
293	async fn classify_rotation_response(response: reqwest::Response) -> RotationError {
294	    let status = response.status().as_u16();
295	    let retry_after = response
296	        .headers()
297	        .get(reqwest::header::RETRY_AFTER)
298	        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
299	        .map(str::to_string);
300	    let body = response.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
301	    if status == 429 {
302	        return RotationError::RateLimited { retry_after };
303	    }
304	    let envelope: Option<serde_json::Value> = serde_json::from_str(&body).ok();
305	    let message = envelope
306	        .as_ref()
307	        .and_then(|v| v.get("message"))
308	        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
309	        .map(String::from)
310	        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
311	            if body.is_empty() {
312	                format!("rotation request returned HTTP {status}")
313	            } else {
314	                body.clone()
315	            }
316	        });
317	    RotationError::RotationFailed { status, message }
318	}
319	
320	/// `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation` on the hosting PDS: stage a fresh replacement key and
321	/// return its `did:key` id.
322	async fn begin_rotation_on_pds(
323	    session: &crate::oauth_client::OAuthClient,
324	) -> Result<String, RotationError> {
325	    let response = session
326	        .post_no_body("/v1/repo-keys/rotation")
327	        .await
328	        .map_err(|e| RotationError::NetworkError {
329	            message: format!("rotation begin request failed: {e}"),
330	        })?;
331	    if !response.status().is_success() {
332	        return Err(classify_rotation_response(response).await);
333	    }
334	    let body: serde_json::Value =
335	        response
336	            .json()
337	            .await
338	            .map_err(|e| RotationError::NetworkError {
339	                message: format!("failed to read rotation begin response: {e}"),
340	            })?;
341	    body.get("signingKey")
342	        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
343	        .map(String::from)
344	        .ok_or_else(|| RotationError::NetworkError {
345	            message: "rotation begin response is missing signingKey".to_string(),
346	        })
347	}
348	
349	/// `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation/complete` on the hosting PDS: submit the signed op for
350	/// plc.directory submission + atomic signer cutover.
351	async fn complete_rotation_on_pds(
352	    session: &crate::oauth_client::OAuthClient,
353	    signed_op: &serde_json::Value,
354	) -> Result<(), RotationError> {
355	    let response = session
356	        .post(
357	            "/v1/repo-keys/rotation/complete",
358	            &serde_json::json!({ "operation": signed_op }),
359	        )
360	        .await
361	        .map_err(|e| RotationError::NetworkError {
362	            message: format!("rotation complete request failed: {e}"),
363	        })?;
364	    if !response.status().is_success() {
365	        return Err(classify_rotation_response(response).await);
366	    }
367	    Ok(())
368	}
369	
370	// ── Imperative shell: build + submit ─────────────────────────────────────────
371	
372	/// Build and locally device-key-sign the repo signing-key rotation operation.
373	///
374	/// Stages a fresh key on the hosting PDS, fetches the DID's audit log (for `prev` +
375	/// current state), composes the rotation op, runs the strict pre-sign guard (which
376	/// proves ONLY the repo key moved, to exactly the PDS-staged key), and signs with the
377	/// per-DID device key. The op is NOT submitted anywhere yet — it is returned for the
378	/// review screen and parked for `submit_repo_key_rotation`.
379	pub async fn build_repo_key_rotation(
380	    pds_client: &PdsClient,
381	    did: &str,
382	) -> Result<SignedRotationOp, RotationError> {
383	    let now =
384	        crate::sovereign_session::unix_timestamp().map_err(|_| RotationError::SigningFailed {
385	            message: "system clock is unavailable".to_string(),
386	        })?;
387	    let store = IdentityStore;
388	
389	    // 1. Full-access session on the hosting PDS (the per-DID session-provider seam).
390	    let session = SessionProvider
391	        .full_access_client(pds_client, &store, did, now)
392	        .await
393	        .map_err(map_session_error)?;
394	
395	    // 2. Stage a fresh replacement key on the PDS. Idempotency note: re-running build
396	    //    stages another fresh key, which simply replaces the previous staged one.
397	    let staged_key_id = begin_rotation_on_pds(&session.client).await?;
398	
399	    // 3. Per-DID device key (rotationKeys[0] for a wallet-custodied identity).
400	    let device =
401	        store
402	            .get_or_create_device_key(did)
403	            .map_err(|e| RotationError::IdentityNotFound {
404	                message: format!("failed to get device key: {e}"),
405	            })?;
406	    let device_key_id = device.key_id;
407	
408	    // 4. Current audit log -> prev + full current state.
409	    let log_json =
410	        pds_client
411	            .fetch_audit_log(did)
412	            .await
413	            .map_err(|e| RotationError::NetworkError {
414	                message: format!("failed to fetch audit log: {e}"),
415	            })?;
416	    let audit_log =
417	        crypto::parse_audit_log(&log_json).map_err(|e| RotationError::InvalidAuditLog {
418	            message: format!("failed to parse audit log: {e}"),
419	        })?;
420	    let current = latest_full_state(&audit_log).map_err(|e| RotationError::InvalidAuditLog {
421	        message: e.to_string(),
422	    })?;
423	
424	    // 5. Compose the proposed op: device key keeps rotationKeys[0], the staged key
425	    //    takes the PDS slot and the atproto verification method; nothing else moves.
426	    let proposed_rotation_keys = vec![device_key_id.clone(), staged_key_id.clone()];
427	    let mut proposed_vms = current.verification_methods.clone();
428	    proposed_vms.insert(
429	        ATPROTO_VERIFICATION_METHOD_ID.to_string(),
430	        staged_key_id.clone(),
431	    );
432	
433	    // 6. Strict pre-sign guard — the security gate.
434	    let inputs = RotationInputs {
435	        device_key_id: device_key_id.clone(),
436	        staged_key_id: staged_key_id.clone(),
437	        current_rotation_keys: current.rotation_keys.clone(),
438	        proposed_rotation_keys: proposed_rotation_keys.clone(),
439	        current_verification_methods: current.verification_methods.clone(),
440	        proposed_verification_methods: proposed_vms.clone(),
441	        current_services: current.services.clone(),
442	        proposed_services: current.services.clone(),
443	        current_also_known_as: current.also_known_as.clone(),
444	        proposed_also_known_as: current.also_known_as.clone(),
445	    };
446	    guard_rotation_op(&inputs)?;
447	
448	    // 7. Sign locally with the per-DID device key.

569	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
570	    did: String,
571	) -> Result<ClaimResult, RotationError> {
572	    let signed_op = {
573	        let pending = state.rotation_state.lock().await;
574	        match pending.as_ref() {
575	            Some(rotation) if rotation.did == did => rotation.signed_op.clone(),
576	            _ => return Err(RotationError::NoPendingRotation),

583	    // submit stays retryable.

585	    if pending.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| r.did == did) {
586	        *pending = None;
587	    }
588	    Ok(result)
589	}

For my design, I'm keeping `build` self-contained without needing a parked operation state — it just stages changes and computes a diff with the recovery key ID for review, while `submit` handles the actual signing, posting, and escrow flow. This means I can skip adding `rekey_state` to `AppState` and leave `oauth.rs` untouched, reducing complexity and risk.

There's a key distinction in the flow: `build` only stages and computes the diff without signing, whereas `submit` does the actual operation building and signing. This differs from `rotate_repo_key` where signing happens during the build phase and returns a signed operation ready to post — but that's because the biometric authorization for SE access happens at a different point in that flow.

The real question is whether the biometric gate in the frontend happens before `build` or before `submit`. Since SE signing on iOS triggers the biometric prompt itself through `LAContext`, I'll mirror `rotate_repo_key`'s approach: `build` does the signing and produces the signed operation, then `submit` posts it. For resumability after a kill, `build` would need to re-run and re-sign, but that's fine since it's idempotent — the staging reuse and stable `prev_cid` mean the same operation gets produced each time.

The cleanest design that mirrors `rotate_repo_key` and handles resumability is to have `build_rekey_cmd` stage shares, fetch state, build and sign the operation, then park the signed operation in `AppState.rekey_state`. Then `submit_rekey_cmd` takes that parked operation (or returns an error if it's missing due to a kill, prompting the frontend to re-run build), posts it, and handles the escrow and share rewrites. Finally, `confirm_rekey_cmd` verifies durability and clears staging. If killed after build, the signed operation is still there for submit to use on resume.

The tricky part is handling the case where the operation already landed on-chain before the kill. On resume, if the recovery key is already in the rotation keys, the guard would reject the build as ineligible, so I need to detect that state and skip straight to the final escrow/share1/refresh steps instead of re-signing.

So the real solution is making `submit_rekey_cmd` the idempotent core that doesn't care about parked state — it reloads the staged set, checks if the recovery key is already on-chain, and if not, builds and signs the rotation operation once. Then it proceeds through escrow, share rewriting, and cache refresh regardless of whether the op was newly posted or already landed.

`build_rekey_cmd` becomes a cheap preview-only operation that stages shares and computes the diff without any signing, so the biometric gate only fires once during submit. This makes the flow much cleaner and resumable — if the user kills the app mid-rekey, reopening just detects the staging slot and jumps back to submit, which converges to the final state.

But there's a wrinkle with the escrow session: it needs stored OAuth tokens for the DID to work, but a wallet-native identity from the ceremony only has a session-token in the keychain, not per-DID OAuth tokens. I need to figure out how `full_access_client` loads those tokens.

Looking at the rotate_repo_key and migration flows, they use `full_access_client` with wallet-native identities, so these identities must have per-DID OAuth token records or sovereign sessions. If the tokens aren't there, `full_access_client` returns NeedsUnlock, and the frontend runs `sovereignLogin(did)` to mint a sovereign session — that's the passwordless path. The recovery key can even bootstrap this sovereign session immediately. For re-key, the device key is still [0] and can sovereign-login, so SESSION_LOCKED just triggers `sovereignLogin(did)` and a retry. That's consistent.

I think the safer approach is to get the session first, then post the op, then escrow — that way if the session is momentarily unavailable, I return SESSION_LOCKED before posting, and on retry the whole flow runs again.

I need to set up the rekey command infrastructure by adding the command names to the union, importing the necessary types, wiring up handlers in the registry, extending the FakeIdentity state with a recovery key field, and creating test scenarios for different key models.

The registry handlers need to validate the identity exists and hasn't already been rekeyed, check that the device is authorized, then either stage a recovery key for the build command or finalize the rotation by inserting the new key and removing old ones for the submit command. The harness state mutates directly since the frontend refetches via getStoredDidDoc/list_identities on load, so that's safe. After submit, rotationKeys becomes 3 keys and rekey_in_progress stays true until confirm clears the staging, which means the recovery key prompt still shows mid-flight. If the user backs out after submit but before confirm, the staging remains set, keeping that state intact.

But there's a problem: if the user kills or reloads after submit succeeds and the frontend advances to the backup screen, on the next home load rotationKeys is 3 (new model) but rekey_in_progress is still true, so the strip shows "Add a recovery key" again. Tapping it runs build, which checks rotationKeys.length === 3 and throws ALREADY_REKEYED—that's a bug in the resume path since the operation already landed.

The real resume should go through submit_rekey (which skips the post if recovery is already on-chain), not build. But the frontend's RekeyReviewScreen calls build first, so resuming after the op landed would hit that error. I need to rethink the resume flow to handle this case properly.

I'm considering two approaches: either detect the in-progress state in RekeyReviewScreen and skip build to call submit directly, or make build_rekey tolerant of a staged recovery key already being present so it can return a preview and let submit proceed.

The cleanest option might be to skip build entirely when a re-key is already in-progress — the frontend should recognize this state and jump straight to a finishing flow that handles escrow and share1 completion.

Actually, I think the real solution is making build_rekey itself resumable. It shouldn't hard-reject when a staged recovery key is already on-chain; instead it should check whether we're in an old-model state (with or without matching staging), a resumed post-op state (where the staged key is already at rotationKeys[1]), or a genuinely new-model account with no staging. Only that last case should trigger AlreadyRekeyed. The tricky part is that build_rekey in rekey.rs has some constraints I need to work around...

Adjusting the guard logic... Refactoring the build_rekey function to check if the recovery key is already present in the rotation keys — if it is, skip the eligibility guard since the operation already landed, and just return the preview with the diff showing the recovery key as added. If it's not present, run the full guard check. This keeps the flow idempotent for resuming operations.

But I'm realizing there's a problem: if there's no staging set and it's a new-model account with three keys already, `load_or_create_for_rekey` would generate a fresh recovery key that isn't on-chain yet, making recovery_present false and triggering the guard, which correctly rejects it as already rekeyed. However, this has the side effect of creating an orphaned staging set unnecessarily. I need to check eligibility before calling load_or_create to avoid staging ineligible accounts in the first place.

So I'm reordering the logic: fetch the current state first, then check if the account is eligible (either old-model with two keys and device at position zero, or has an in-progress rekey staging set) before attempting to load or create shares. This way, new-model accounts without an active rekey get rejected immediately without generating unnecessary staging data. Checking if staging exists for the DID, and if not, validating that we're in the old two-key model before proceeding. Then loading or creating the shares for the rekey operation, and if the recovery key isn't already on-chain, running the full guard to ensure the device is at the first position and we have exactly the device and PDS keys.

The logic handles all the cases correctly: fresh rekey with no staging passes the length check and runs the guard; resuming before the operation lands reuses staging and runs the guard since recovery isn't on-chain yet; resuming after it lands skips the guard since recovery is now on-chain; genuinely new model attempts get rejected; and did:web DIDs are blocked upfront. The submit operation already handles the case where the operation has landed. Refactoring build_rekey...

66	             release_pending_until = NULL \

81	/// once the account has a client-generated Share 2 in `recovery_escrow`, the
82	/// legacy column is dead material that must not linger in backups. Returns
83	/// whether a non-NULL value was actually cleared, so the caller records the
84	/// void only when there was material to void. Idempotent: a repeat call, or a
85	/// call for an account that never had a legacy share (created after the

91	where
92	    E: sqlx::Executor<'e, Database = Sqlite>,

95	        "UPDATE accounts SET recovery_share = NULL WHERE did = ? AND recovery_share IS NOT NULL",
96	    )
97	    .bind(did)
98	    .execute(executor)
99	    .await?;
100	    Ok(result.rows_affected() == 1)
101	}

3	// Functional Core: the strict additive re-key guard and the review-diff computation (pure).
4	// Imperative Shell: build_rekey / submit_rekey / confirm_rekey (share generation + network +
5	//                   Keychain + signing) and their Tauri command wrappers.
6	//
7	// This is the "re-key migration" for existing OLD-MODEL accounts (MM-411). Every account
8	// created before the ceremony inversion carries a server-generated 2-of-3 split of a secret
9	// bound to nothing: the shares protect nothing, and the server saw all three at generation.
10	// Such an account's `rotationKeys` are the 2-key `[device, PDS]` array — no recovery key. The
11	// account's real safety net is unchanged from today: the device key itself.
12	//
13	// The re-key moves the account onto the client-generated recovery model, exactly like a fresh
14	// ceremony but against an existing identity:
15	//   1. Generate a NEW recovery seed client-side, derive its recovery key, split 2-of-3 (v2
16	//      envelopes), staged in a per-DID Keychain slot BEFORE any network call.
17	//   2. Device-key-sign a PLC rotation op INSERTING the recovery key at `rotationKeys[1]` — the
18	//      device key stays at `[0]`, the existing PDS key shifts to `[2]`. Nothing is removed.
19	//   3. `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share` with the new Share 2 (the server deposits it and voids the
20	//      dead legacy `accounts.recovery_share` in the same transaction).
21	//   4. Overwrite the per-DID Keychain Share 1 slot with the new Share 1 (verified read-back).
22	//   5. Walk the user through saving the new Share 3 (frontend reuses ShamirBackupScreen), then
23	//      refresh the cached DID doc and tear down the staging slot.
24	//
25	// ADDITIVE-ONLY SAFETY. The device key never leaves `rotationKeys[0]`; the new shares are staged
26	// before the PLC op; escrow deposit follows it. A failure at any step leaves the account no less
27	// recoverable than today (device key only), and a resumed re-key converges to the same terminal
28	// state — every network/Keychain step below is idempotent. There is no window in which the
29	// account is worse off. Old shares are VOIDED by the re-key, not merely rotated — the honest
30	// framing, since they never protected anything.
31	//
32	// Unlike the sovereign repo-key rotation (which routes its op through the PDS so the commit
33	// signer cuts over atomically), a re-key never changes `verificationMethods.atproto` — the PDS
34	// key is the SAME key, only repositioned — so the wallet submits this op to plc.directory

rewrite Keychain Share 1, walk the user through saving the new Share 3 (reusing
`ShamirBackupScreen`). Until re-key, the account's real safety net is unchanged from

**As built (MM-411).** The wallet's `rekey.rs` composes the existing MM-407 seams:
`share_ceremony::load_or_create_for_rekey` (a **per-DID** staging slot, so re-keying one
identity can never abandon or orphan another's staged seed) → `build_did_plc_rotation_op`
signed by `per_did_sign_closure` → `post_plc_operation` → `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share`
(over a `SessionProvider` full-access session; the server nulls `accounts.recovery_share`
in the same transaction and records `legacy_voided` in the escrow audit detail) → refresh.
The three commands are `build_rekey` (preview + stage), `submit_rekey` (idempotent
post→escrow→Share 1→refresh), and `confirm_rekey` (Share 3 saved → staging teardown).
Two deliberate divergences from the sketch above: (1) the re-key writes a **per-DID**
`recovery-share-1:{did}` Keychain slot rather than the app-global `recovery-share-1` the
create/migration flows still use — clobbering a sibling identity's Share 1 would drop
*that* identity below its baseline, which the "no intermediate state is worse off" AC
forbids; unifying create/migration onto per-DID slots is a tracked follow-up. (2) Resume
is driven by the per-DID staging slot (`rekey_in_progress`), so an interrupted re-key
whose PLC op already landed (identity reads as new-model) still resurfaces the prompt and
finishes escrow/Share 1 idempotently. The re-key op is device-key-signed, so `plc_monitor`
already treats it as authorized (no tamper alert) — asserted by a test, not new code.

Re-key migration: move existing old-model accounts onto client-generated shares + recovery rotation key (MM-411)

lazy, per-DID re-key that moves such accounts onto the client-generated model.

removed) → PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share → rewrite per-DID Keychain Share 1 →
reuse ShamirBackupScreen for the new Share 3 → refresh. Additive-only and
idempotent/resumable at every step: the device key never leaves [0], so no
intermediate state drops recovery below the pre-re-key baseline. A calm,
seal-toned "Add a recovery key" strip on the home surface prompts only old-model
did:plc identities (never new-model or did:web).

in the same transaction and record legacy_voided in the escrow audit detail.

plc_monitor already authorizes the re-key op (device-key-signed) — asserted by a
test, not new code.

Phase 2–3 bridge of the [key-recovery epic (MM-405)](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-405); design `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-key-recovery-from-shares.md` §7. Builds on MM-407 (ceremony inversion, `d1ad28c7`) and MM-408 (escrow storage, `9bbb1cba`), both in the base.

## What

Every pre-existing account carries the **old recovery model**: a server-generated 2-of-3 split of a secret bound to nothing — the shares protect nothing and the server saw all three at generation. This adds the **lazy, per-DID re-key** that moves such accounts onto the client-generated model, and voids the dead legacy material server-side.

## Wallet (`rekey.rs`, new)

Composes the existing MM-407 seams — no new crypto:
- **Detect** old-model per identity: did:plc + authoritative doc has a 2-key `rotationKeys` array (`isOldModelRecovery`). did:web and new-model (3-key) identities are never prompted.
- **Prompt** a calm, seal-toned "Add a recovery key" strip on the home surface (deliberately *not* the critical/alert palette — an upgrade, not an incident).
- **Run** `build_rekey` (generate seed client-side + stage per-DID + preview) → `submit_rekey` (device-key-signed PLC rotation op inserting the recovery key at `rotationKeys[1]`, device stays `[0]`, PDS shifts to `[2]`, **nothing removed** → `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share` → rewrite per-DID Keychain Share 1 → refresh) → reuse `ShamirBackupScreen` for the new Share 3 → `confirm_rekey` (staging teardown).
- **Additive-only + resumable**: the device key never leaves `rotationKeys[0]`, shares are staged before the PLC op, escrow follows it. Every network/Keychain step is idempotent, so an interrupt at any step converges to the same terminal state and **no intermediate state drops recovery below the pre-re-key baseline** (device key only). Resume is driven by the per-DID staging slot, so an interrupted re-key whose op already landed still resurfaces and finishes escrow/Share 1.

## PDS

On a successful escrow deposit, null the dead legacy `accounts.recovery_share` in the **same transaction** and record `legacy_voided` in the escrow audit detail. Nulling is KEK-safe (the `RecoveryShares` rewrap sweep already skips NULL rows). No new migration — dropping the column is a tracked follow-up.

## Deliberate divergences from the sketch (see design §7 "As built")

1. **Per-DID Share 1 slot** (`recovery-share-1:{did}`) rather than the app-global slot the create/migration flows still use — clobbering a sibling identity's Share 1 would drop *that* identity below baseline. Unifying create/migration onto per-DID slots is a tracked follow-up.
2. Re-key posts its op to plc.directory **directly** (like migration/recovery), not via the PDS: it never changes `verificationMethods.atproto`, so there is no commit-signer cutover to make atomic.

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ **Old-model did:plc**: full re-key ends with 3 rotation keys, a new Share 3, Share 1 overwritten, legacy column NULL. *Driven end-to-end live in the browser harness.*
- ✅ **did:web + new-model never prompt** — verified live (`rekey-mixed` scenario) and in unit tests.
- ✅ **Interrupt-and-resume** converges on the same terminal state; no intermediate state below baseline — unit + integration tests.
- ✅ **`plc_monitor` treats the re-key op as authorized** (device-key-signed → no tamper alert) — asserted by a new test; no code change needed.

## Tests / checks

- PDS: `recovery_escrow` DB + route tests (legacy null-out, `legacy_voided` detail) — green.
- Wallet Rust: `rekey` guard/diff/eligibility (13), per-DID `share_ceremony` staging, `plc_monitor` re-key authorization — green. Full wallet suite 455 passed.
- Frontend: `isOldModelRecovery` unit tests + full harness flow (detect / build→submit→confirm / resume idempotence / did:web + new-model + non-root rejection) — 41 passed. `pnpm check` clean.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean on both crates; touched files rustfmt'd.
- Regenerated the wallet IPC docs reference (4 new `invoke` commands).

New IPC surface: `build_rekey_cmd`, `submit_rekey_cmd`, `confirm_rekey_cmd`, `rekey_in_progress_cmd`; `OAuthClient::put` added for the escrow `PUT`.
EOF

Let me flag the one out-of-scope issue I uncovered as a follow-up task, since it's a genuine multi-identity correctness gap in the *existing* create/migration flows:

input.title: Unify create/migration onto per-DID Share 1 slots
input.prompt:
The create ceremony (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `perform_did_ceremony` ~line 594) and the account-migration flow (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/migrate.rs` ~line 733) both write the recovery Share 1 to a single **app-global** Keychain slot literal `"recovery-share-1"`, and `confirm_share_backup` (lib.rs ~line 637) reads that global slot. In a multi-identity wallet this is a latent bug: creating or migrating identity B overwrites identity A's Share 1, dropping A's share-based recovery.

MM-411 (the re-key flow, `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/rekey.rs`) deliberately introduced a **per-DID** slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` (see `recovery_share1_account`) to avoid this. This follow-up should unify create + migration onto the same per-DID scheme:
- Write `recovery-share-1:{did}` in `perform_did_ceremony` and `migrate.rs`.
- Make `confirm_share_backup` per-DID (it currently takes no DID arg — this touches the create-flow frontend contract in `apps/identity-wallet/src/routes/+page.svelte` `confirmBackupAndContinue`, which must thread the DID like the re-key epilogue's `confirmRekeyBackup` already does).
- Consider a one-time migration of any existing global `recovery-share-1` slot to the per-DID slot for the wallet's primary identity.
- The recovery ceremony (MM-410, when built) must read the per-DID slot.

Context: this was noted as a tracked follow-up in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-key-recovery-from-shares.md` §7 ("As built") and in the `recovery_share1_account` doc comment in rekey.rs.
input.tldr: The create and migration flows write recovery Share 1 to one app-global keychain slot, so in a multi-identity wallet each new/migrated identity clobbers a sibling's Share 1. MM-411's re-key already uses a per-DID slot; this unifies the older flows onto it.

content.text:
MM-411 is complete. Here's what shipped and why it holds together.

## Summary

The re-key migration moves pre-existing "old-model" accounts (a server-generated Shamir split of a secret bound to nothing) onto the client-generated recovery model — lazily, per-DID, and additively.

**PDS** — [`recovery_escrow.rs`](crates/pds/src/routes/recovery_escrow.rs): on a successful escrow deposit, the dead legacy `accounts.recovery_share` is nulled in the *same transaction*, with `legacy_voided` recorded in the audit detail.

**Wallet Rust** — [`rekey.rs`](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/rekey.rs) (new): `build_rekey` → `submit_rekey` → `confirm_rekey`, composing MM-407's seams — client-side seed generation (per-DID staging), a device-key-signed rotation op inserting the recovery key at `rotationKeys[1]`, escrow `PUT` (new `OAuthClient::put`), per-DID Share 1 rewrite, cache refresh.

**Frontend** — a calm seal-toned "Add a recovery key" strip ([`IdentityListHome.svelte`](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/components/home/IdentityListHome.svelte)) and a review→backup→success flow reusing `ShamirBackupScreen`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The safety property is structural, not procedural.** Because the device key never leaves `rotationKeys[0]` and the old shares protected nothing, *every* intermediate state (op-landed-but-escrow-pending, escrow-done-but-Share-1-stale) is exactly as recoverable as the pre-re-key baseline — the device key. That's what lets each step be independently idempotent and the whole thing resume-safe without a durable state machine.
- **Resume detection rides on-chain state + a keychain slot, not a progress enum.** `isOldModelRecovery` (2-key doc) catches un-started re-keys; `rekey_in_progress` (per-DID staging slot) catches ones whose op already landed and now read as new-model — closing the gap where `build_rekey` would otherwise reject with `ALREADY_REKEYED`.
- **`plc_monitor` needed zero code.** Its authorization check is "did *our* device key sign this op?" — signature only, indifferent to what the op does — so a device-signed re-key is authorized for free. I proved it with a test rather than adding logic.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Verification (all four ACs)
- **Live in the browser harness**: drove the full old-model re-key end-to-end (3 rotation keys, new Share 3, staging torn down, strip gone), and confirmed the strip appears *only* on the old-model did:plc identity — never the new-model or did:web ones.
- **Automated**: PDS null-out tests; 13 re-key guard/eligibility tests; per-DID staging tests; the `plc_monitor` authorization test; `isOldModelRecovery` + a full harness integration test (build/submit/confirm, resume idempotence, negative cases). Full wallet suite 455 passed, 41 frontend tests passed, `pnpm check` clean, `clippy -D warnings` clean.

## Notes
- **Deliberate divergence** (documented in design §7 "As built"): re-key uses a **per-DID** `recovery-share-1:{did}` slot rather than the app-global slot the create/migration flows still use — clobbering a sibling's Share 1 would violate the "no state worse off" AC. I filed a follow-up chip to unify create/migration onto per-DID slots (that's a pre-existing multi-identity bug in those flows, out of scope here).
- No new PDS route (Bruno parity unaffected); regenerated the wallet IPC docs reference for the 4 new commands so `docs-check` passes.

content.text:
The fix is pushed and I'm waiting on the re-run. Here's where things stand:

**CI failure diagnosed and fixed.** The PDS gate failed at `ticket-ref-check` — I'd left four `MM-411`/`MM-300`/`AC` references in `.rs` comments, which the repo forbids (traceability belongs in `docs/`, not source). I reworded all four to describe the *why* in system terms, confirmed the gate now passes locally (`✓ no ticket/AC references in Rust source`) and that fmt stays clean, and pushed as `f90f54b9` to [PR #340](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/340).

This was a fast-fail *before* clippy/test ran on CI, and those steps were already green locally, so the re-run should pass — I'm polling the gate in the background and will report when it reaches a terminal state.

I also recorded the gotcha to project memory so I grep `.rs` files for ticket refs before pushing next time.
